newsitem.title: USA: Deere profits jump, revises sales estimates upward.
newsitem.headline: Deere profits jump, revises sales estimates upward.

text.p: Deere & Co., the agricultural and construction equipment giant, Tuesday said its earnings soared 17 percent to a record in the latest quarter on strong worldwide retail demand.
The Moline, Ill.-based company also revised its sales forecast upward.

Deere said it earned $319.5 million, or $1.25 a share, in its fiscal second quarter ended April 30, up from year-ago earnings of $272.7 million, or $1.04 a share. Earnings exceeded the First Call consensus estimate of $1.15 a share.
Revenues jumped to $3.52 billion from $3.08 billion.
"Overall, the outlook for the company's businesses remains very positive," said Deere Chairman Hans Becherer.
Deere said it now expects its 1997 sales to grow by 8 percent from a year earlier, up from a previous forecast of a 6 percent rise.
It said the third-quarter outlook is also better than expected and that it sees a sales gain of 10 percent from a year ago.
"The remainder of 1997 should benefit from a growing global economy, healthy agricultural markets and generally higher levels of farmer confidence," Becherer said.
He said that improving dietary trends and rapid income growth in many developing nations are stimulating demand for farm commodities, and grain and oilseed prices remain at relatively strong levels.

"Industry retail demand for construction equipment is strong and is expected to remain at similar levels throughout 1997 as favourable economic growth, rising incomes and low inflation rates continue to result in good housing demand," Becherer added.
Deere's stock hit a new 52-week high of $52 Tuesday and was up $2.375 at $51.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
"The broad-based nature of their optimism was somewhat of an upside surprise for people," Lisa Shalett, analyst at Sanford C. Bernstein, said.
Deere's outlook gave a boost to the stocks of its competitors, Caterpillar Inc., Case Corp. and AGCO Corp..
"The influences that are driving those revenue performances at Deere should be readily applicable for Case as well," J. Blair Brumley, analyst at Dain Bosworth Inc., said.

Racine, Wis.-based Case shares rose $1.75 to $57.50, while Caterpillar, the Peoria-based capital equipment maker, reached a fresh 52-week high of $97.875, both on the NYSE. Caterpillar was up 50 cents at $96.75 in late trading.
Duluth, Georgia-based AGCO Corp., an agricultural equipment maker, rose 87.5 cents to $30.50, near its year's high of $31.625.
Roger Sit, analyst at Goldman Sachs, said many of the capital equipment makers' stocks are trading at a discount due to market assumptions that the current U.S. economic cycle is nearing its end.
Using an analogy of a baseball game, Sit said Deere's comments might help convince the market the economic cycle that has helped boost these companies is not about to end.
"I'm in no way advocating that we're in the first inning in the ballgame, but we're not in the ninth inning," Sit said.
